tldr: The joint absolute-risk and finite-sample honest-length frontier is matched over the entire bounded Hölder-CDF class, including atoms and degenerate outcomes. Its common rate is \(\min\{1,(n\epsilon)^{-1/2}+\min[n^{-4\alpha/(4\alpha+1)}\epsilon^{-(2\alpha+1)/(4\alpha+1)},(n^2\epsilon)^{-\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}]\}\), without logarithmic factors. Finite score crossings give a total original-record estimator, and a deterministic radius gives a connected interval with at least \(0.90\) coverage at the actual sample size. The same-record known-propensity rate is \(\min\{1,(n\epsilon)^{-1/2}\}\). An explicit minimum of two level--smoothness penalties characterizes exactly when learning propensity preserves that order, separately for risk and length; uniform preservation over all levels holds exactly when \(\alpha\ge1/3\).
gap: \cite{AiLintonMotegiZhang2021} supplies efficient causal loss estimation, and \cite{ZhangLiuZhang2026HOGeneralTreatment} already supplies higher-order implicit-root theory.
